source: Rebuilt by pipeline.replay_publications from the collector’s own position captures of 26 September 2026, 11:54–12:06 UTC (37 captures, each checked against the SHA-256 in its name), matched against the server’s catalogue of that morning — the captures of tests/recorded/fleet-journey-change-192.json. One Diamond (BNDB) route-65 vehicle, YY73OYL, on journey 1244 throughout: it reported at 11:55:10, then nothing for 445 s, then at 12:02:35, 172 m on; the published trail reaches back 240 s, so the report after the silence arrived with none from before it. Every other vehicle removed; every publication kept, so its absences are as they were.

policy.basis: Measured publication delay p50 30s / p95 40s on the retained sample. Expiry exists because that sample carried positions up to 23.1 hours old.

measured.caveat: Report intervals are bounded by the cadence of the responses we hold, so they describe our observation cadence, not the operator's publication rate. Operators are required to publish every 10-30 seconds.

notes: Positions are reports, not continuous tracking. Every position in this file is an observed fix kept exactly as received: nothing here is interpolated, smoothed or predicted.

The page may draw a clearly labelled estimate of where a selected bus has got to since its last report. Estimates are computed on the device, bounded by measured behaviour, and are never published here, stored, or counted as observations.
A position older than the expiry threshold is withheld and counted, because the feed demonstrably carries positions that are hours old.
No arrival time is offered. Progress toward a stop is shown only where a timetabled service pattern is matched, and is counted in stops along that pattern, not minutes.
A reported position shows a direction only where the vehicle reported a bearing; a missing or unreadable bearing is stated, never estimated from movement.
Each bus carries up to six earlier reports from the last four minutes of the same journey (its trail), each pointing at the source file it came from.

notes: Positions are reports, not continuous tracking. Every position in this file is an observed fix kept exactly as received: nothing here is interpolated, smoothed or predicted.

The page may draw a clearly labelled estimate of where a selected bus has got to since its last report. Estimates are computed on the device, bounded by measured behaviour, and are never published here, stored, or counted as observations.
A position older than the expiry threshold is withheld and counted, because the feed demonstrably carries positions that are hours old.
No arrival time is offered. Progress toward a stop is shown only where a timetabled service pattern is matched, and is counted in stops along that pattern, not minutes.
A reported position shows a direction only where the vehicle reported a bearing; a missing or unreadable bearing is stated, never estimated from movement.
Each bus carries up to six earlier reports from the last four minutes of the same journey (its trail), each pointing at the source file it came from.

policy.basis: Measured publication delay p50 30s / p95 40s on the retained sample. Expiry exists because that sample carried positions up to 23.1 hours old.

measured.caveat: Report intervals are bounded by the cadence of the responses we hold, so they describe our observation cadence, not the operator's publication rate. Operators are required to publish every 10-30 seconds.
